Anthropogenic land use/ cover change (LUC) have profound impact on N cycling, but the magnitude of such impacts depends on the intensity and type of LUC, and that the intensity of the LUC is what drives changes in N dynamics.

1) the replacement of native ecosystems by exotic forests has increased the supply of nutrients and organic matter to the watershed lakes, 2) this increase in nutrients and organic matter is related to the increase of N availability and 3) this increase in N availability is the result of an increase in the supply of N to the lake, which is related to the replacement of native grasslands by exotic forests.

the replacement of native forest and grasslands with tree plantations of Monterey pine Pinus radiaata and eucaliptus Eucaliptus globulus during the 1970s in the Matanzaz watershed, Chile, increased the amount of nutrients and organic matter transferred from the terrestrial to aquatic ecosystems.

the role that anthropogenic activities have played on N cycling in the Matanzás lake system over the last two hundred years.
the impact of anthropogenic activities on the nutrient and carbon cycles of a mediterranean watershed lake system in central Chile.

the timing, magnitude and intensity of anthropogenic land uses/cover changes on nutrient cycling, which has important implications for understanding and predicting the effects of future land use/cover change on the global N cycle and its impacts on terrestrial and aquatic ecosystem functioning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the impact of anthropogenic land cover and land use changes on N dynamics in mediterranean coastal watersheds is highly variable, depending on the intensity and magnitude of these land use changes and their timing in the watershed.
the timing of the Great Acceleration is not the same in all ecosystems.
the intensity of LUCCA and not the mere presence of such activities is the main driver of changes in the nutrient and organic matter cycles in these mediterranian coastal watershed systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the timing and intensity of land use changes in this watershed have a profound effect on the magnitude and timing of N availability to aquatic systems.
(i) The Matanzas watershed is an example of a mediterranean lake system that has been impacted by human activities for centuries.

(a) the impact of land use/cover change on nutrient dynamics is not necessarily immediate but rather it depends on the intensity, magnitude, and duration of the changes; and (b) the impact of such changes is not necessarily linear, but rather it is dependent on the interaction of the different land use/cover types and the magnitude of the changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intensity of land cover change is a major driver in the magnitude of nutrient transfer from terrestrial to aquatic ecosystems.

the magnitude and intensity with which humans have modified the landscape and its associated ecosystems is the most important determinant in understanding how human activities affect the biogeochemistry of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
the intensity of anthropogenic land uses/cover changes in mediterranean waters is the most important driver of N availability, and thus, the main driver of the ecological state of these systems.
